text: The correction decision of the exception loop is served on the write-off base as POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/correction-decision under /api/recovery/writeoff/v1, with CorrectionRequest in and WriteOffCorrection out, and takes the capability area Write-off and posting with right A, because a correction is a decision on the write-off.
why: TSD S7 T-A.1 publishes two operations for the module and the legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E6-024 repeats those two rows for the loop, so no source names an operation for the correction; the legacy permission table gives the module right A to RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM and RW-FINANCE and right C to RW-WRITEOFF and RW-CREDITAD, and a decision on the write-off is the A of the two.
read: TSD S7 T-A.1 and T-A.2; API Specification v4 operation postWriteOffsWriteoffidCommitteeDecision; legacy RWB-E6-024 Endpoints and Permission checks; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-13; context pack naming rules
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6024-APP sections 1, 4, 12.1 and 13; RWB-S7-E6024-CON sections 2, 7 AC1 and AC4, 8 BR12, 12.1 and 19
confirm: Solution architect, the rwb-writeoff tech lead and the access owner of rwb-access, before the contract is tagged
impact: SCR-27 and the case workspace call the correction on the write-off base; a renamed path or element inside major version 1 does not break them, and a wrong right closes the loop to the roles that work it

text: The loop's owner and the correction task's time limit are reference and rule values: the owner is the write-off committee member role, the legacy persona and the primary role of the feature, on right A; the task is raised through the human-task template of the workflow kit and appears on the case workspace of rwb-case, on right C; and no time limit is written in code, so the template's timer takes its target from a reference row at run time and REQ-S7-004 stays open until C&R publish the two values.
why: R-WO-24 gives the owner as Owner to confirm with C&R and the timer as to confirm with Credit Administration, the States sheet labels WRITEOFF_EXCEPTION as Write-off exception, owner to confirm, and the FSD says of the feature that this loop has no owner today; REQ-S7-004 requires one named owner and a time limit, so both values are needed and neither may be invented as a business value.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-24, R-WO-41 and R-WO-44 and the States sheet; FSD S7 A2.12.1 and A2.12.3.3; legacy RWB-E6-024 Story, Endpoints and Permission checks; TSD S7 T6.1; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S7-004; Temporal and Drools Design slide 12 (human task with SLA)
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6024-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 BR6, 9, 12.2, 12.6, 13 and 18; RWB-S7-E6024-CON sections 2, 7 AC3 and AC4, 8 BR12, 11 and 12.6
confirm: C&R, Credit Administration and the solution architect, before wave 4 starts
impact: The loop opens with a named role and no service level until the values are published, and a wrong default owner sends the correction task to the wrong team

text: The correction vocabulary is the event column of the three exit rules, CORRECTION_REPOST, CORRECTION_RETURN_TO_SCAN and CORRECTION_REFER_TO_COMMITTEE, copied character for character, and it is the only enumeration the contract publishes, because no list of values exists for the module.
why: TSD S7 T3.2 is an empty list-of-values table and the published CommitteeDecision enumeration of approve, reject and defer cannot carry a correction, while the three exits of WRITEOFF_EXCEPTION name their event in the routing logic; taking the codes from there publishes no invented value.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-44, R-WO-45 and R-WO-46 and the States sheet; TSD S7 T3.2; API Specification v4 schema CommitteeDecision
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6024-APP sections 4, 7, 8 BR6 and BR10, 9, 12.1 and 15; RWB-S7-E6024-CON sections 7 AC2 and AC5, 8 BR7, 11 and 12.1
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-decision rule owner, before the contract is tagged
impact: The three corrections are testable by name and a fourth correction would need a new rule and a new event before it could be accepted

text: retry_count and the retry limit are not columns of write_off and not fields of any list: the count is the posting step's fact of the same WriteOffWorkflow, RWB-S7-E6021-APP, and the limit is a rule fact of the WO package read from rwb-decision at its version in force, so neither is copied into rwb_writeoff and neither becomes a constant, a schema default or a branch.
why: R-WO-24 fires on retry_count at or above the retry limit, TSD S7 T3.1 gives write_off eleven fields and none of them is a count or a limit, the FSD field catalog repeats the same eight fields, and the posting retries are R-WO-22 and R-WO-23 in the posting feature, so the count belongs to the posting step and the limit to the package.
read: TSD S7 T3.1 and T4; FSD S7 A2.9 and A2.12.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-22, R-WO-23 and R-WO-24; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6024-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 8 BR3, 11, 12.2, 12.7 and 13; RWB-S7-E6024-CON sections 7 AC4 and AC7, 8 BR12, 11 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect, the rwb-decision rule owner and the rwb-writeoff tech lead, before the first posting retry is built
impact: No migration is needed for the loop and a change of the retry limit is a rule version, not a release of this service

text: The case read, the four case-move answers and the correction task raise are consumed from P3 rwb-case with operation names that no source publishes; on the workflow boundary the moves are the stage outcome the parent CaseWorkflow applies, and the assignment row of DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016 is written by the case workspace and never by this service.
why: recovery_case, task and assignment are work-management facts of the case service in the target, the context pack gives S7 a single table, and the connection matrix has no REST row from S7 to P3, so the boundary is the workflow outcome and the workspace task; no source names the operation of a case move or of a task raise.
read: Context pack ownership rows and connection-matrix row S7; TSD S7 T4, T5.2 and T6.1; LDM v8 rows DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016 and the assignment entity; legacy RWB-E6-024 Data table
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6024-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 8 BR4, 11, 12.2 and 13; RWB-S7-E6024-CON sections 7 AC3, 8 BR4, 11 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-case tech lead, before the contract is tagged
impact: The raise and every correction are provable on the move and the task answer without a table grant, and the workspace remains the only writer of the assignment

text: The other two entries to WRITEOFF_EXCEPTION belong to the payment and reconciliation slices by their subject: R-WO-41 to RWB-S7-E6027-APP and R-WO-43 to RWB-S7-E6023-APP; this story claims R-WO-24 and the three exits only, and both unclaimed entries are recorded because neither appears in an FSD feature rule table.
why: The States sheet counts three rules into the state, the FSD carries R-WO-24 in A2.12 and A2.6 and R-WO-44 in A2.9, and R-WO-41 and R-WO-43 appear in no feature table, while the payment and reconciliation features are the two slices whose subject they name; leaving them unowned would leave two entries of a state this story works without a story.

impact: A questioned or unreconciled write-off enters the same state this story works, and the two entry rules are carried by the slices whose data they use rather than duplicated here
